objective: 0.3.0 pi 11/12: Make T3 Code the primary interface for HolyAgent on pi and integrate deeply with it: T3 runs pi through `pi --mode rpc`, HolyAgent uses T3's own dialogs, browser and visual tools, enables T3's beneficial settings, adds computer use through Cua Driver, and keeps only the T3 tools it needs.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "also I want holyagent pi to be compatible with t3 code"; scope "In 0.3.0"; then "t3code shall be the primary interface for the pi integration, so we will deeply integrate with it. that means we can rely on its integrated browser, computer use, as well as enable anything beneficial we can from it globally or locally". The maintainer implements 0.3.0; this Intent records the plan.

Maintainer, 2026-11-07: implement 0.3.0 now, every part except the dropped auto-mode gate (pi 8/10); test with unit tests and recorded or synthesized fixtures only, no live Kimi runs; merge each PR once it is reviewed and green.

Facts (research assignment-0mw6r54ng-kg9r, sources pingdotgg/t3code docs/user/providers-pi.md and PR #7211): T3 Code runs the user's own pi install as a built-in provider (Early Access, pi 0.80.5 or newer, enabled in T3 Settings) through `pi --mode rpc` over stdio JSONL, rejects launch args that change mode or session, carries pi's models, auth, extensions, skills and context files, and injects its own MCP bridge extension (prefix mcp__t3-code__).
HolyAgent pi works in rpc mode (ctx.mode "rpc", hasUI true) and sets no launch args for mode or session.

Decided (maintainer: "I want tthem to run with t3code's dialogs/ui, no weird tui stuff"): under T3, every HolyAgent interaction uses only the RPC extension UI that T3 renders (select, confirm, input, editor in T3's composer; notify to the work log; setStatus near the composer) and never custom(), widgets, footer, titles or theme calls; the ask-user and todo tools (rpiv) follow this, with a HolyAgent adapter where a package relies on custom() TUI rendering.

Decided (maintainer: "Require Full access"): HolyAgent threads in T3 run in T3's Full access mode, consistent with the full-access default; the docs and the setup check say so, and HolyAgent warns when a T3 session runs in Supervised or Auto-accept edits, where every extension tool call prompts and background specialists could stall.

Decided (maintainer: "pi's stuff"): specialists report back through @tintinweb/pi-subagents' own new-turn trigger, not T3's delegate_task; a recorded fixture of T3's RPC traffic verifies that a completion notice arriving after agent_settled starts a new root turn in T3.

Decided (maintainer: "t3code can delegate stuff with their mcp, can we disable whatever is unnecessary from it?"; research assignment-0mw6r9zxs-l85j): HolyAgent keeps T3's html_render, html_preview, preview_*, t3_preview_* and device_* tools (its visual route and device access) and deactivates T3's orchestration tools (orchestrator_capabilities, delegate_task, task_status, task_cancel, create_threads, t3_thread_*, schedule_task, list_scheduled_tasks, delete_scheduled_task, t3_pending_request and any other mcp__t3-code__ tool outside those families) with pi.setActiveTools filtered by prefix from getAllTools(), applied once at session_start before the first request and reapplied on before_agent_start and session_tree, with a tool_call block as backstop; there is no T3 setting for this.

Prompt caching: the active tool set is fixed at session_start and not toggled mid-session, so the cached prefix holds (pi docs: setActiveTools changes provider tools; models without mid-conversation system messages take a cache miss per change).

To verify during implementation: the T3 release containing PR #7211; the exact preview_* set; whether T3's bridge re-adds tools after HolyAgent filters them; whether deferred tools stay discoverable through tool_search once excluded; pi 1.5.0 against T3's agent_settled and clear_queue assumptions; whether the rpiv packages use custom().
Tests: CI covers T3 with recorded fixtures of `pi --mode rpc` traffic inside the existing CI jobs, as the other pi tests do.

T3 Code is the primary interface for HolyAgent on pi: the docs lead with T3 Code, the plain pi terminal stays supported (maintainer: "Keep it supported"), with T3-only features falling back or reported unavailable there and CI covering both the terminal and T3's rpc mode, and HolyAgent relies on T3 features rather than rebuilding them (research assignment-0mw6rgzog-2rb3).

Browser: the visual roles use T3's integrated browser (preview_status, preview_open, preview_dialog, preview_navigate, preview_resize, preview_set_appearance, preview_snapshot, preview_act, preview_evaluate, preview_wait_for, preview_recording_start, preview_recording_stop) and html_render and html_preview; the fixed tool set pins these names, since on pi 0.99 and newer they are deferred behind tool_search.

Computer use (maintainer: "cua driver"; research assignment-0mw6rlor5-3o9f): T3 provides none for pi, so HolyAgent adds Cua Driver (trycua/cua, MIT; macOS 14+, Windows 10/11, Linux X11 or XWayland preview) through the existing pi extension @amaster.ai/pi-computer-use, pinned and moved by deps:update; it runs in standard permission mode with the extension's confirmations off (maintainer: "Full access, no prompts"), and only Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual get its tools; the driver is the copy the extension bundles (no separate install; the bundled version moves with the extension pin), and setup walks through the macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.

T3 device access (simulators, device_* tools) is enabled where the host supports it (macOS with Xcode, or the Android SDK); whether pi reaches device_* is verified during implementation (root default from "enable anything beneficial").

T3 settings (maintainer: "Setup writes them"): once the implementation verifies the format of T3's settings.json under T3CODE_HOME (default ~/.t3), holyagent setup for pi writes the beneficial T3 settings (pi provider enabled, worktrees, context meter, device access) globally or as per-project overrides, with an undo; when the format is unverified or unsupported, setup prints the T3 Settings steps instead.

Relied on as they are: T3's model and effort pickers, checkpoints and rollback (pi session files), skills menu, worktrees, terminal, diff and PR flow; T3's scheduled tasks stay usable from T3's UI while their agent tools stay deactivated.

Maintainer (verbatim): "the context meter is the little context indicator? don't set it." Setup does not write T3's context meter, and the config has no key for it; the rest of the T3 settings setup writes are chosen by the maintainer from a full list of T3 settings.
